graphql_authorization.summary: Aimeos disclosed improper GraphQL access control that allowed an editor to manage services through the GraphQL admin API beyond what the corresponding administrative UI permitted.
graphql_authorization.description: The maintainer advisory documents an authorization mismatch in the Aimeos GraphQL administration interface: an editor role can perform service-management operations through GraphQL that are not allowed through the intended JQAdm permission model. The relevant condition is an authenticated GraphQL operation crossing the caller's effective authorization boundary, not schema discovery.
graphql_authorization.selection_basis: official maintainer advisory selected before scoring using WSTG GraphQL and authorization-enforcement semantics

source_map_exposure.summary: gov-bb's security audit documented sourceMappingURL-driven arbitrary .map-file disclosure in its PostCSS build chain, with source maps capable of exposing original source code and sensitive build outputs.
source_map_exposure.description: The project security-audit issue records a vulnerable PostCSS dependency that auto-loads previous source maps referenced by sourceMappingURL. Attacker-controlled CSS can cause arbitrary .map files to be read outside the intended directory. The issue explicitly identifies sourcesContent and original source code, secrets embedded in build artifacts and sensitive build outputs as exposed information, making the security condition an obtainable source-map/debug artifact disclosure rather than a marker-only observation.
source_map_exposure.selection_basis: fresh project security-audit issue selected before scoring using WSTG-INFO-05 source-map and original-source disclosure semantics

unsafe_api_consumption.summary: rickbot's maintainer documented reachable aiohttp HTTP-client vulnerabilities including credential leakage when a remote response redirects the client across origins.
unsafe_api_consumption.description: The project-owner security issue establishes that discord.py uses aiohttp as an HTTP and WebSocket client and enumerates reachable client-side defects. Among them, a remote redirect to a different origin can cause per-request cookies or Cookie/Proxy-Authorization credentials to cross the host boundary. This is an external HTTP-client trust-boundary failure in which the client consumes a redirect response and carries credential material into the redirected origin rather than re-validating the changed remote-service boundary.
unsafe_api_consumption.selection_basis: fresh project-owner security issue selected before scoring using OWASP API10 unsafe-consumption semantics with WSTG-INFO-10 external-service trust-boundary mapping

websocket_authorization.summary: layout-orchestration documented a WebSocket control channel with no authentication or authorization, allowing anonymous control operations until the upgrade path was gated.
websocket_authorization.description: The project-owner security review states that both HTTP and WebSocket surfaces lacked authentication and authorization. The throttle and point WebSocket control channel already issued hardware commands, so an anonymous caller could cross the intended access-control boundary and influence sensitive state. The required fix explicitly covers WebSocket upgrade authentication and acceptance requires unauthenticated WebSocket upgrades to be rejected, demonstrating the authorization bypass boundary rather than generic WebSocket presence.
websocket_authorization.selection_basis: fresh project-owner security review selected before scoring using WSTG WebSocket and authorization-enforcement semantics
